answer: Trust propagates through a bounded-length random walk on the attestation graph, so an identity’s influence depends on reachable, independently supported paths rather than its raw number of endorsements. An adversary can forge identities, but a sybil cluster separated by a sparse cut has low conductance: few trusted edges carry probability mass across its ridge. Thus, even if every internal edge shares the same pigment, min-cut bounds limit the cluster’s aggregate voting weight.
